title: Docker Lab Run Flow
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Docker Python Lab Type
Runnable Code Block
Lab Sandbox
Troubleshooting
MkDocs configuration
description: A vis-network path from a Docker Python lab's Run button through docker-lab.js, the local service on port 5001 and a fresh container to the output area; break it with one of five failures and diagnose the missing part from the symptom.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Diagnosing why a Docker Python lab fails to run
learningObjectives: The learner will diagnose why a lab fails to run by identifying which part of the path from browser to container is missing.
prerequisites: Runnable Code Blocks and the Lab Sandbox section of Chapter 11
Basic familiarity with a browser developer console

accessibility.notes: Information panel is an aria-live region; the Break it menu and Diagnose first checkbox are native form controls

controls.label: Five parts of the run path
controls.purpose: Show each part's role and one thing that can break it, or answer a diagnosis

controls.label: Run clicked, code sent, container started, text returned, output displayed
controls.purpose: Show what travels along each arrow

controls.label: Break it
controls.purpose: Choose one of five failures or a mystery failure

controls.label: Diagnose first
controls.purpose: Show only the symptom until the learner clicks the broken part

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Process path explorer with failure scenarios and click-to-diagnose
keyQuestions: Which part wrote the 'Cannot connect' message, and what does that tell you?
How do the two 'nothing happens' failures differ?
Why does input() fail in the sandbox?
commonMisconceptions: The Python code runs in the browser
A lab that shows an error message has a broken script
Reloading the page starts the Docker service
assessmentOpportunities: Explaining the clue that separates two similar symptoms
